audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 1 and 2 gave the stage to Nautilus in both layers while their own whys read 'stays skill-based' and 'still a coin-flip decided by who lands their engage'. The packet chart reads Skill for both, and the mirror audit already committed to Skill at levels 2 and 3.
audit.why: Nautilus has no damage pattern at levels 2-3 — his whole threat is gated on a 14s Dredge Line landing. Neither side is favoured until his first tank item.
audit.corrected: Rows 1 and 2 set to Skill in both layers as matched pairs. Rows 5 and 6 stay Nautilus, matching the packet and the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: Depth Charge was described only as 'a point-and-click knock-up', and Titan's Wrath never appeared at all despite being the shield that decides the first-item stage.
audit.why: Depth Charge is 825 range on 120/100/80 and knocks up everything along its path before stunning the target — the reason a hook into it is unsurvivable. Titan's Wrath is a flat 12s shield at every rank, so the trade window is right after it expires.
audit.corrected: Real range and cooldown written into spikes[1]; Titan's Wrath and its flat 12s cooldown added to spikes[2] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Staggering Blow was mentioned nowhere in the writable text, and dontsFull[1] ('Eat his passive root chain') carried a body about burning mobility that had nothing to do with the passive.
audit.why: Nautilus's first attack against each target roots them. Against a melee who must walk in, that means his opening auto is hard CC before any ability is cast — it is what actually starts the chain the don't is warning about.
audit.corrected: Staggering Blow's root named in spikes[0], breakdown.cooldowns, dontsFull[1].d and report[5].t, with Dredge Line's 14s / 1150 range and Riptide's 7s so the trade gap is concrete.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carried no numbers and treated Dredge Line as the only tracked cooldown.
audit.why: Dredge Line 14/13/12/11/10, Titan's Wrath flat 12, Riptide 7/6.5/6/5.5/5, Depth Charge 120/100/80. Riptide's short cooldown is why the gap to trade in is the missed hook, not the spent Riptide.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, mid, spikes[0] and report[5].t.

edits.before: Nautilus is a low-damage lane bully whose threat is entirely his Dredge Line hook plus Riptide slow; if you respect the hook and space around Q Darkin Glaive, the early trades are a skill-based coin-flip decided by who lands their engage.
edits.after: Nautilus is a low-damage lane bully whose threat is Dredge Line (Q, 14s at rank 1) plus Riptide's slow — and Staggering Blow roots you on his first attack, so even a walk-up auto is CC. Respect the hook and that first auto and the early trades stay a coin-flip.

edits.before: His R Depth Charge is a point-and-click knock-up that chains into his full CC combo, so his all-in and skirmish threat jumps here; hold E Golden Onslaught and don't stand in a spot where a hook-into-ult can start.
edits.after: Depth Charge (R) is point-and-click at 825 range, 120s at rank 1, and stuns you at the end of its path straight into his combo. Hold your E for after it lands, not before, and never stand where a hook can start it.

edits.before: With his first tank item Nautilus becomes a durable roaming CC threat who beats you in an extended fight and enables ganks; the lane tilts his way as his utility outweighs your solo damage.
edits.after: With his first tank item Nautilus becomes a durable roaming CC threat who wins extended fights; Titan's Wrath (W) is a flat 12s shield, so trade after it pops rather than into it, and keep every fight short.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 remain even and hook-dependent: respect his Riptide slow and Dredge Line so a single mistake doesn't chain into his combo, and tax his mana with pokes when he shoves. Whoever wins the engage battle wins the trade.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 remain even and hook-dependent: Dredge Line is 14s at rank 1 while Riptide is back in 7s, so the gap worth trading in is a missed hook, not a spent Riptide. Tax his mana when he shoves — whoever wins the engage battle wins the trade.

edits.before: - Nautilus Dredge Line: matchup-defining — His only engage. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Dredge Line (Q): matchup-defining — 14s at rank 1, 1150 range. Dodge it, then commit inside the gap. - Titan's Wrath (W): a flat 12s shield. - Staggering Blow: his first attack on you roots.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Staggering Blow roots on his first attack — that is what starts it.

edits.before: Track Nautilus's Dredge Line (Hook): His only engage. Dodge it. When it is down — Combo + R him.
edits.after: Dredge Line: 14s, 1150 range, his only engage. Staggering Blow roots on his first attack on you.

notes: The kit file tags Dredge Line with a 'terrain — creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes' flag, but Riot's description only says colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus toward it. Nautilus creates no wall, so I did NOT write anything about the hook denying Zaahen's E dash. Zaahen ability names again avoided: the Nautilus-side mirror used The Darkin Glaive / Aureate Rush / Grim Deliverance at its own stated Medium confidence, so I left the one existing 'Q Darkin Glaive' string in place but replaced the fabricated 'E Golden Onslaught' with a slot reference rather than picking a name.
